Queen-led GraphQL uses LangGraph for state transitions, confirmation, locking, failure routing, and recovery while enforcing independent Judge and Final Arbiter roles. C wins: synchronous chat uses Worker, Tunnel, and local runtime; async runner control plane keeps identity, heartbeat, lease, result, and evidence.
Worker validates access and signs runtime calls. Runtime verifies HMAC, then calls Ollama or provider APIs and streams SSE back.

/agent/graphql is the only orchestration entry for real tasks. LangGraph executes the state graph boundary. Queen proposes an editable DAG; accepted assignments and the current revision must be confirmed before start, then the run locks the graph. Judge and Final Arbiter remain independent agents with isolated context.

GraphQL keeps the mandatory stages intact, applies cost-priority ranking with quality gates, auto-adds rescue policy, and triggers red-team review for high-risk or low-judge-score paths.

The three-choice pool filters by access, capabilities, license/tag metadata, health, and score history, then deduplicates by modelTag. New zero-score models receive exploration boost; old low-score models are retired.
User-imported Ollama agents are private and owner-only by default. Public Edge calls pass a public caller scope, so local agents require an authenticated owner runtime scope before selection.

The three-choice pool filters by access, capabilities, license/tag metadata, health, and score history, then deduplicates by modelTag. New zero-score models receive exploration boost; old low-score models are retired.
